title: Launch Runbook: Autonomous Decision Grid and Rapid Escalation Templates
body:
Purpose:
This runbook is a living working doc that combines an autonomy decision grid (who can do what, when), concrete KPI gates for each launch tranche, and copy-ready escalation/communication templates. Use this for pilots, staggered canaries, and GA ramps for hosted API and Dedicated offerings.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Reduce meeting overhead and speed incident responses by mapping actions to autonomy tiers and explicit KPI gates.
- Focus areas: traffic ramp choreography, quick rollback play, stakeholder notifications, and short post-mortems.
- Current status: draft; needs SRE threshold confirmation and legal review for EU private deploy notes.

Autonomy tiers (decision grid):
- Tier 0 (Free Run): low-risk ops (feature flags, non-user-visible A/B changes). Owners: PM + Eng. Conditions: pass smoke, no infra alerts for 48h. KPIs: no increase in support signal; token-cost variance < 8%.
- Tier 1 (Guarded Run): medium changes (config, batching, minor model parameter swaps). Owners: PM + Eng + Ops approval. Conditions: canary at 1-5% for 24h with stable p95 and error budget. KPIs: p95 within 15% of baseline, error-rate < 0.5%.
- Tier 2 (Controlled Run): high impact (model variant replace, significant traffic shifts >10%). Owners: cross-functional signoff (PM, Eng lead, SRE, Support). Conditions: explicit canary exit checklist completed. KPIs: p99 < threshold, customer-impact tickets minimal, cost delta within agreed band.
- Tier 3 (Lockdown): immediate freeze and escalation triggered (security, data, or critical reliability regression). Owners: Incident Commander and executive-notified responders. Actions: stop ramp, rollback to last-known-good, open incident doc.

KPI gate definitions (how we measure):
- Service Success Rate: percentage of non-error API responses. Canary target: >= 99.5%; GA target: >= 99.9%.
- p50/p95/p99 latency: measured by route and model. Example baseline for small models: p99 < 600ms (adjust per model).
- Error Budget Consumption: fraction of allowed errors used. If consumption > 30% in 1 hour -> escalate to Guarded Run.
- Token Economy: daily cost-per-1k-tokens vs forecast. Exceeding forecast by > 12% requires review.
- Quality Delta: automated eval set score drift (semantic-similarity) < 1.5% vs baseline.
- Customer Signals: tickets/1k users and DSAT; threshold for escalation: 5x baseline or > 3 high-severity tickets in 24h.

Monitoring and alerts (practical rules):
- Dashboards required before any canary: per-route throughput, latency percentiles, error types, token burn, and model-level quality sweep.
- Alert tiers: Advisory (inform), Action (owner should act), Critical (declare incident).
  - Advisory example: p95 above baseline +20% for 15m.
  - Action example: error-rate > 0.75% for 10m or p99 > 2x baseline for 5m.
  - Critical example: data-integrity failure, p99 > 3x baseline for 5m, or sustained SLO violation with customer impact.
- Integrations: PagerDuty for page routing, Slack incident channel auto-created by ops-bot, and automated scorecard emails to stakeholders.

Escalation choreography (step-by-step):
1) Alert fires -> ops-bot posts to #launch-ops with summary and owner tags.
2) Product-ops triage within 10 minutes to categorize tier and assign Incident Commander if needed.
3) Tier 1: 60-minute mitigation window (config tweak or limited rollback).
4) Tier 2: 30-minute mitigation window, cross-functional war-room, consider traffic backoff to safe baseline.
5) Tier 3: immediate rollback and executive notification.
6) Post-incident: 48h RCA assigned; 72h change freeze for non-critical changes.

Communication templates (copy/paste):
- Slack short (ops channel):
  [LAUNCH UPDATE] {feature} | env={env} | status={tier} | IC={name} | action={next steps} | ETA={eta}
- Stakeholder email subject:
  "{Feature} activation update — {env} — {YYYY-MM-DD} — {status}"
  Body skeleton: TL;DR, what happened, KPIs impacted, immediate action taken, next update ETA, owners.
- Customer-facing note (pre-approved): short apology + known impact + mitigation and ETA for resolution. Marketing to sign off if external.

Prelaunch checklist (must be green before any traffic ramp):
- Smoke tests and integration tests pass in staging.
- Canary plan documented with duration, traffic steps, and rollback criteria.
- Dashboards live and validated (sample traffic, alert simulation done).
- PagerDuty + on-call roster configured for launch window.
- Rollback artifact validated via dry-run.
- Support snippets and escalation e-mails prepared in Zendesk.
- Privacy/security review complete for target deployment mode (public/ dedicated/ private).

Canary exit & GA ramp criteria (recommended):
- Minimum observability window: 72 hours with no Action/Critical alerts.
- KPI drift window: key metrics within guardrails for 48 consecutive hours.
- Customer signal: no critical tickets and DSAT within acceptable range.
- Team readiness: on-call/SRE roster confirmed and handoff doc complete.

Staffing and handovers (practical suggestions):
- For canaries >10% traffic, require one SRE standby and daily PM/Eng handoffs during first 72 hours.
- Handover notes: current traffic %, notable trends, open actions, and phone/slack contacts (store contacts in secure roster doc).
- Regional overlap: schedule 2-hour overlap for shift changes to avoid blind spots.

Post-launch cadence (first 7 days):
- Daily automated scorecard (uptime, p99, error-rate, cost burn, top-two tickets).
- Quick sync: 15-minute PM+Eng stand at the top of each day for first 3 days.
- Day 7 decision: continue ramp, stabilize with slower ramp, or rollback. Document decision and rationale.

Ownership & outstanding actions (who owns what):
- SRE: finalize numeric alert thresholds for medium/large models (owner: Luca Moretti; due: 2025-02-10).
- Legal: confirm EU private deployment residency notes and template text (owner: Priya Shah; due: 2025-02-12).
- Product-ops: script for automated canary ramp and backoff (PR: github:redwood-inference/rollouts#94).

Notes & provenance:
- This runbook synthesizes prior rollout learnings and aims to reduce synchronous touchpoints by clarifying decision authority at each tier.
- Keep this doc concise; link to detailed runbooks and PagerDuty playbooks rather than copying them in.

Revision history:
- 2025-01-14: initial draft (Maya Thompson).
- 2025-01-27: added escalation choreography and communication templates after tabletop exercise.
- 2025-02-03: incorporated SRE feedback and moved to in_review.
